snippet.description:
When Your UPSC Dream Is Bigger Than the Struggle.

The UPSC journey is not easy. There will be long hours, self-doubt, setbacks and moments when giving up feels easier. But when the dream matters enough, the struggle becomes part of the journey.

This video is for every UPSC aspirant who is still preparing, still working, and still choosing to move forward despite the challenges.

Your dream is bigger than one bad day, one failed attempt, or one difficult phase.

Keep going. Keep working. Keep believing in the journey.

If you are preparing for UPSC CSE 2027, UPSC CSE 2028 or beyond, let this be your reminder to stay consistent and keep moving.

snippet.description:
How should you make revision notes for UPSC? AIR 25 Bhavika Chopra shares a practical method that helped her prepare smarter, not harder. Instead of writing everything, she explains why your notes should contain only the things you tend to forget, how PYQs can help identify those gaps, and why concepts and facts should be revised differently. If your notes keep getting bigger but your revision isn't improving, this strategy can completely change the way you prepare.

Bhavika Chopra’s journey is a story of persistence and smart course correction. A graduate in Economics (Honours) from St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, she initially secured AIR 476 in UPSC CSE 2023 and was selected for the Indian Postal Service. Instead of settling, she chose to reattempt with a clearer strategy and stronger focus.

Hailing from Chandigarh and academically strong since school, Bhavika also worked at Ernst & Young before fully committing to UPSC preparation. Her transition from Economics to Sociology, combined with disciplined preparation, helped her secure AIR 25 in UPSC CSE 2025, making her journey both relatable and inspiring for aspirants.
